principle: A shipped template's verification command must WORK ON THAT STACK'S DEFAULT SCAFFOLD, and must be able to both PASS and FAIL. A command that cannot fail is a blind gate; a command that cannot pass is a brick. Where a command depends on a tool the default scaffold lacks, that dependency is recorded explicitly rather than left implicit.
note: One entry per stack, so an UNCHANGED stack is ADJUDICATED rather than absent. `after` equals `before` where the existing value was already correct. `corrections` lists every key changed for that stack, including keys other than `test`.

entries.justification: `dotnet test` is the first-party test driver and ships with the SDK. Correct as-is.
`go test ./...` is the toolchain's own runner and needs no dependency. Correct as-is.
Primary language is python (framework.primary: python, measured — NOT typescript). pytest is the de facto runner. Test command correct as-is; the `syntax` key was a brick and is corrected below.

corrections.defect: BRICK — a check that can never pass
corrections.evidence: `python3 -m py_compile` with no arguments exits 2: 'the following arguments are required: filenames'. Measured 2026-09-20. `compileall -q .` measured exit 1 on a tree containing a syntax error and exit 0 on a clean tree.

entries.justification: `mix test` ships with Elixir and a generated Phoenix app includes ExUnit. Correct as-is. DEPENDENCY RECORDED: `type` (mix dialyzer) requires the `dialyxir` dep and `lint` (mix credo) requires `credo`; neither is in a default `mix phx.new`. Kept because both are the ecosystem's standard choices, but a customer without them gets a failing command.

Django's own built-in runner is `python manage.py test` (unittest); pytest requires pytest-django. Kept as pytest because the template also declares pytest as the language test_framework, and changing one without the other would split the SSOT. DEPENDENCY RECORDED: requires pytest-django on a default `django-admin startproject`.

entries.justification: CHANGED. Minitest is Rails' default test framework and `bin/rails test` works on a fresh `rails new` with no added gems. `bundle exec rspec` requires adding rspec-rails to the Gemfile, so the shipped command FAILED on a default Rails app. DEPENDENCY RECORDED: `type` (bundle exec sorbet tc) requires the sorbet gem; Ruby has no default static type checker, so this key cannot be satisfied by a default scaffold at all.

corrections.defect: BLIND GATE — a check that can never fail
corrections.evidence: `ruby -c` with no file argument reads STDIN: on empty stdin it printed 'Syntax OK' and exited 0 without inspecting a single project file (and blocks on a TTY). Measured 2026-09-20. The replacement measured exit 1 on a tree containing a syntax error and exit 0 on a clean tree.

entries.justification: `cargo test` ships with the Rust toolchain. Correct as-is.

The template declares a Maven project, and Spring Initializr emits the `mvnw` wrapper, so `./mvnw test` runs without a global Maven install. A Gradle project would use `./gradlew test`, which is why this is recorded rather than assumed. DEPENDENCY RECORDED: `lint` (./mvnw checkstyle:check) requires the checkstyle plugin configured in pom.xml; it is not in a default Initializr project.
The template declares a SwiftPM layout (paths.source: Sources, source_dirs: [Sources]), for which `swift test` is the correct runner. Correct as-is.

corrections.defect: TOOLCHAIN MISMATCH — the command requires an artifact the declared layout does not describe
corrections.evidence: `xcodebuild build` requires an .xcodeproj/.xcworkspace, but this template declares a SwiftPM `Sources/` layout (paths.source: Sources, source_dirs: [Sources]) and uses `swift test`/`swift build` for its other keys. One stack cannot be SwiftPM for two keys and Xcode for a third. This is a DESIGN JUDGEMENT, not a mechanically proven failure: the template's internal inconsistency was demonstrated, not that `xcodebuild build` fails for a real swift-ios customer.
corrections.plant_machinery_updated: The literal was the target of three anti-vacuity plants proving pattern-scanner Check 43 can fail (gate-registry.json: the swift-template failpoint, the map-literal failpoint, and the template-verification-vr-map-drift vitest guard). All three patterns and both oracles were re-pointed to the new literal, Check 43's expected command set was updated, and BOTH plants were re-run and proven to still drive Check 43 RED naming 'swift build -c release' — with the clean tree still opening. Changing the command without this would have left the gate green and no longer able to fail.

entries.justification: The Nest CLI scaffolds a `test` script in package.json, so `npm test` resolves on a default project. Correct as-is.

Kept as `npm test`: it is runner-agnostic and resolves to whatever the project declares. DEPENDENCY RECORDED: `create-next-app` does NOT scaffold a `test` script, so `npm test` fails on a bare Next.js app until the customer adds one. Recorded rather than changed, because inventing a runner here would guess which one the customer chose.
